questions.question:

“Please allow me to leave now,” Ritika said to her teacher.

options.text: Ritika requested my teacher to allow her to leave now.
Ritika requested her teacher to allow her to leave then.
Ritika requested her teacher to allow me to leave now.

questions.solution:

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the Direct speech and we need to change this into indirect speech.
 
• The given reported speech is an imperative sentence. Hence, we need to use an infinitive.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

You could put your money to good use.

options.text: Your money is being put to good use.
Your money could have been put to good use.
Your money could be put to good use.
Your money has been put to good use.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Your money could be put to good use"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and we need to change this in the passive voice.
 
• The given sentence uses the past tense "could" and the object of the sentence is "your money" which will become the subject of the sentence.
 
• We need to use the following structure- Object (in active voice) + be + V₃ + Subject (in active voice)
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3 i.e. "Your money could be put to good use."**

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

B. The host welcomed him warmly.

C. At last he arrived at the beautiful city.

D. Great preparations were made for Amir of Isfahan’s journey to Shiraz.

• Overall all given four sentences are talking about **Amir**
 
• We need to find an opening statement among these four sentences.
 
• "**Option A is starting with But" **which is used to show the contrast situation.
 
• It simply means that "**Sentence A" can not be an opening statement.**
 
• In sentence B "**Him" ** is used. "**Him" **is a pronoun (**Possessive Adjective Case)** that is used instead of a Noun.
 
• It simply means that there should be a Noun before **Sentence B, **with the help of this we can eliminate options.
 
• Sentence C starts with "**At last"**
 
• **The sentence **which starts with at last **can not be an opening statement** based on meaning.
 
• As "Sentence A, Sentence B, Sentence C' are not the opening statement. Statement D is the opening Statement
 
• In the sentence D There is a noun named "**Amir".**
 
• **We use pronouns to avoid repetition of Noun**
 
• In sentence D 
 
 
• Preparations were made
 
 
 
• In Sentence C
 
 
• He arrived at the Beautiful city.
 
 
 
• In Sentence B
 
 
• The host welcomed **him(Used for Amir)**
 
 
 
• **Generally, **Hosts are requested to rest but here it is showing that contrast so option A is the last sentence.
 
 
 
• So the correct meaningful and coherent Sequence is **DCBA**

**So the correct passage is-***** ****D. **Great preparations were made for Amir of Isfahan’s journey to Shiraz. **C.** At last, he arrived at the beautiful city. **B**. The host welcomed him warmly. **A.** But instead of asking the guest to rest, he said, “I have arranged to take you for Shikar.”*
